instagram_carousel.caption:
Punta Cana is on the shortlist. Here is what to settle first if you are planning from Australia.

Legal or symbolic. You can marry legally through a Dominican civil registry office, or marry legally in Australia with a celebrant and hold a symbolic ceremony on the sand. If you marry in the Dominican Republic, foreigners provide a birth certificate, a passport and a certificate of single status, legalised and apostilled in their country of origin, and any document not in Spanish needs a translation. Allow time for each step. Both of you must attend in person, and overseas marriages cannot be registered in Australia. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

The weather. On the World Meteorological Organization's 1961 to 1990 climate normals for Punta Cana, supplied by ONAMET, February and March are the driest months and October is the wettest. There is no cool season to wait for, so ceremony time and shade matter in every month.

Hurricane season. The US National Hurricane Center gives the Atlantic hurricane season as 1 June to 30 November. As at November 2026, Smartraveller notes that tropical storms and hurricanes can happen in other months, so a covered option and good travel insurance matter in any month.

Your guests. As at November 2026, Smartraveller says every guest must buy a tourist card on arrival and complete the electronic entry and exit form. Entry conditions can change at short notice, so guests should check with the nearest Dominican embassy or consulate. Put it all in a guest travel note that goes out with the save the date.

Before you sign, ask any venue how many weddings it holds on your date, what it allows on the sand, what shade sits over the guests' seats, how older guests reach the ceremony, and to see the covered wet weather option, not just hear about it.
